sovereign_country.strategic_role: 拉美美元金融中枢、私人利益基金会（PIF）与运河船舶登记

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Authorized Economic Operator (AEO) Certification and Security Auditing

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid - Civil Law tradition (Código Civil and Código de Comercio) with a U.S.-influenced corporate statute (Law 32 of 1927) and a modern AML/CFT overlay consistent with FATF standards
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Panama-United States Trade Promotion Agreement (TPA, in force 2012)
Panama-European Union Association Agreement (trade and investment framework)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law 23 of April 27, 2015 (AML/CFT statutory framework, as amended by Law 70 of 2019 and Law 53 of 2018); Law 129 of July 24, 2020 (centralized Beneficial Ownership Register); Executive Decrees 374 of 2021, 175 of 2022 and 120 of 2023 (UBO filing obligation, deadlines and penalties); UAF Resolution 2022-04 (customer due diligence and PEP screening guidance). The UBO register is administered by the Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) under the Ministry of Economy and Finance.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport or national ID of each shareholder and ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport authority or civil registry of the country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport of each proposed director and corporate officer
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport authority of the country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Original bank reference letter and source-of-funds statement for each UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Financial institution of the country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney appointing the Panamanian incorporation agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary of the country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing or certificate of incumbency if the sole shareholder is a corporate entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry of the home jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: UBO declaration form (Formulario de Beneficiario Final) for the DGI register
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary of the country of origin for signature recognition, then filed with DGI Panama
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization abroad plus Hague Apostille (when executed outside Panama)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based screening of all UBOs, directors, officers, and authorized signatories against the OFAC SDN and consolidated sanctions lists, the UN Security Council consolidated list, the EU consolidated list, and Panamanian national designations published by the Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF). Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) is mandatory for any politically exposed person (PEP), including a 24-month post-employment cooling-off period. All screening results, filings, and supporting records must be documented and retained for a minimum of five years under Law 23 of 2015 and UAF regulations.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.urns_and_legal_entity_identifier_sop: Not applicable at pre-incorporation stage; obtain the LEI code, if required by counterparties, within 90 days after incorporation.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá - online naming reservation service (Dirección de Personas Jurídicas) at www.registro-publico.gob.pa
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Spanish is the official statutory language. Corporate names must be expressed in Latin script and must include a corporate suffix such as 'Sociedad Anónima', 'S.A.', 'Inc.', 'Corp.', 'Corporation', or 'Limited'. Foreign-language names are indexed and transliterated to Spanish for registry search purposes; any constitutive document in a foreign language must be translated into Spanish by a Panamanian sworn public translator before registration.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the name is rejected, the applicant may file a written 'Recurso de Reconsideración' with the General Directorate of the Registro Público within five business days of written notification, attaching a revised name list. If reconsideration is denied, an 'Recurso de Apelación' may be pursued before the same General Directorate, and finally a 'Demanda Contencioso-Administrativa' before the Sala Tercera de lo Contencioso-Administrativo of the Corte Suprema de Justicia. A fresh reservation request may be filed immediately after rejection. Prior ministerial authorization is obtained through the corresponding regulator before reservation where the proposed name contains a sensitive token.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted. The S.A. must appoint a resident agent who maintains a registered office address in Panama; a physical operating presence is not required for incorporation. However, given the declared AEO and supply-chain audit scope (ISIC 7020), a substantive professional office in Panama is strongly recommended to evidence commercial substance and to support a future AEO authorization application.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low for ordinary administrative use, approximately 10% per annum for a standard registered-office address. This rises to 100% mandatory on-site verification and periodic audit if the company applies for Authorized Economic Operator status before the Dirección General de Aduanas.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name clearance search and name reservation certificate
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff for Certificado de Búsqueda y Reserva de Nombre

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market fee under Law 32 of 1927 drafting practice

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory registration fee schedule for sociedades anónimas

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO register initial filing (Registro de Beneficiarios Finales)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: DGI fee schedule for RBF filings under Executive Decree 374 of 2021

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Corporate records kit and stock certificate ledger
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for legalized corporate kit

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Resident agent and registered office service, first year
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Annual retainer market benchmark (includes registered office address)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing per-document tariff for sworn translation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille and consular legalization of UBO, ID, and bank reference bundle

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Hague Apostille Convention fee plus courier handling

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: PEP, OFAC, UN, and EU consolidated sanctions screening of all parties
Pre-incorporation AML/CFT legal opinion and due diligence certification
AEO and supply-chain compliance gap analysis (ISIC 7020 scoped, optional)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: International customs/AEO advisory practice, Panama desk
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed-fee advisory benchmark for pre-incorporation substance and AEO readiness

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley No. 32 de 26 de febrero de 1927 (General Law on Corporations / Sociedades Anónimas), as amended by Ley 23 de 2015 and related decrees; applicable provisions include Articles 8–71 governing the formation, capital, governance, and resident agent requirements of the Panamanian S.A., supplemented by the Commercial Code and Public Registry regulations.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá (Public Registry of Panama), Dirección General, Sección de Personas Jurídicas / Registro Mercantil.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Pública de Constitución / Pacto Social (public deed of incorporation and articles of association) accompanied by the resident agent acceptance and first directors' acceptance, filed for inscription in the Public Registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Panama imposes no statutory minimum paid-up capital and no escrow deposit requirement; the articles must declare an authorized capital and share classes, and issued shares may be subscribed with payment in cash or in kind at the board's determination. The first board resolution records the authorized and issued capital as declared subscribed and fully paid.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, at this first meeting of the Board of Directors of the Corporation duly convened under Law 32 of 1927, as amended: The authorized and issued capital is declared subscribed and fully paid, with share certificates ordered for immediate issuance; The registered office shall be maintained as stated in the Articles of Incorporation, and [Resident Agent Firm] is ratified as resident agent; The following officers are elected: [President], [Secretary], and [Treasurer], to serve until successors are validly chosen; Officers are authorized to execute all filings, open corporate bank accounts, and take any action required for the RUC registration, municipal operating permit, and commencement of AEO supply-chain compliance auditing and security consulting services. Approved by unanimous written consent.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Ventanilla de Certificados de Nombre / Online 'Sede Electrónica' portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit three proposed corporate names in descending order of preference through the Public Registry's online portal or service window. Pay the certification fee and obtain the Certificado de Nombre, which is valid for 30 days and must be attached to the incorporation deed.
required_dossiers: Name certificate application form
Copy of the applicant's passport or national ID
Proof of payment of the name certification fee (approximately US$25)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the preferred name is rejected for conflict or similarity, resubmit the next proposed name or file a reconsideration request with the Public Registry; corrections in the same session generally carry no additional fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Panamanian attorney or incorporated corporate services firm registered under Ley 23 de 2015; engagement subsequently recorded at the Registro Público de Panamá.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute the resident agent agreement with a licensed Panamanian lawyer or law firm. The resident agent accepts service of process, maintains the registered office address, and executes the acceptance clause on the deed of incorporation.
required_dossiers: Signed resident agent agreement
Copy of the resident agent's professional license (idoneidad)
KYC and ultimate beneficial owner identification form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the appointed agent becomes unavailable prior to registration, appoint an alternate resident agent and amend the deed accordingly; post-registration changes require a formal amendment (reforma) filed with the Public Registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of the Public Deed of Incorporation (Pacto Social)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notaría Pública (Panamanian notary) with corporate counsel drafting the deed.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Escritura Pública de Constitución containing the corporate name, purpose clause expressly covering management consultancy, AEO compliance auditing, supply-chain security advisory, and related services, term, authorized capital, director appointments, registered office, and resident agent clause. Shareholders sign before the notary.
required_dossiers: Valid name certificate
Resident agent agreement and acceptance
Passport or ID of each founding shareholder
Draft articles of incorporation (Pacto Social)
Proof of payment of notarial fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: On notarial observation, correct the defective clause by a contemporaneous rider or re-execute the deed; the notary issues certified copies for subsequent registry filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Inscription at the Public Registry of Panama
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Sección de Personas Jurídicas / Registro Mercantil.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the notarized deed with the resident agent acceptance, first directors' acceptance, and fee payment receipt at the Public Registry. The registry assigns a Ficha and Asiento number and, upon satisfactory verification, records the legal existence of the S.A.
required_dossiers: Original notarized public deed of incorporation
Certified copy of the deed
Resident agent appointment and acceptance
Receipt of payment of registration, folio, and stamp fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a 'razón' (formal query), cure the cited defect within the stated statutory term, typically 10 working days; if the term lapses, resubmit the corrected document and pay the applicable reason fee for re-entry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Corporate Registration Certificate, Books, and Personería Jurídica
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá and licensed Panamanian public accountant for book legalization.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon inscription, obtain the certified Certificado de Personería Jurídica and registry excerpt. Legalize the corporate books (share register, board minutes book, and accounting ledger) at the Public Registry and issue signed share certificates in accordance with the first board resolution.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the registered deed
Receipt of payment of certificate issuance fees
Physical corporate books submitted for stamping
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If certificate issuance is incomplete, request a duplicate from the registry after settling any differential fee; re-present uncertified books once stamping fees are paid.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration with the Dirección General de Ingresos (RUC)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas — DGI en Línea online portal and taxpayer service offices.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the S.A. in the Registro Único de Contribuyentes and obtain the RUC number. Select ISIC 7020 for the principal activity, confirm the territorial-source taxation basis, and apply for electronic invoicing authorization as required for future billing of consulting and audit services.
required_dossiers: Certificado de Personería Jurídica
Registered deed or certified registry excerpt
Copy of resident agent identification and authorization
Completed RUC registration form
Passport copies of foreign shareholders and officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RUC application is queried for classification issues, resubmit the corrected form with a supporting explanatory letter and the proper ISIC code; escalate to the DGI taxpayer attention unit if the issue persists.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Operating License (Aviso de Operación and Patente)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alcaldía del Distrito de Panamá — Dirección de Patentes y Licencias / 'Tramita Panamá' municipal one-stop window.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Aviso de Operación indicating the registered office as the commercial establishment. The municipal patent is assessed on the declared capital or projected gross receipts; pay the proportional municipal tax and obtain the displayed operating license certificate.
required_dossiers: RUC certificate
Certificado de Personería Jurídica
Completed municipal Aviso de Operación application
Lease agreement or property title for the registered office
Fire safety inspection receipt from the Cuerpo de Bomberos
Copy of the legal representative's ID
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipality objects to the declared taxable base or documentation, file a corrective declaration at the municipal attention window or submit an administrative appeal to the Alcalde within five working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Bank Account Opening and Payment Rail Enablement (Wire Transfer and Wise)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Panamanian banks regulated by the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá and Wise Business onboarding.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a corporate operating account at a licensed Panamanian bank by presenting certified corporate documents, completing KYC and beneficial ownership disclosure, and designating authorized signatories. Request SWIFT international wire transfer capability and configure Wise Business for multi-currency receivables in support of the target payment rails.
required_dossiers: Certified registration excerpt and Personería Jurídica
RUC certificate
Notarized corporate board resolution designating signatories
Completed bank KYC and beneficial ownership forms
Passport copies and professional references of beneficial owners
Proof of registered office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If enhanced due diligence is requested, provide notarized identity documentation and source-of-funds declarations; if the bank declines, submit the same qualified file to an alternate licensed bank or escalate to the bank's compliance committee.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias (MICI) — Dirección General de Comercio; no industrial factory registration applies to ISIC 7020 office-based consultancy and audit activities.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Aviso de Operación y Patente Municipal (municipal commercial operating license) with optional MICI commercial registry notice; no manufacturing or industrial establishment permit is required for AEO supply-chain compliance auditing.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAmbiente) — Dirección de Evaluación de Impacto Ambiental
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt (Category III — administrative, non-industrial activity) under Decreto Ley No. 2 de 2007; no full EIA report is required for consultancy and audit offices, although a low-impact environmental registration form may be requested by the municipality in connection with the operating license.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater, VOC, or hazardous emissions are generated by the activity; office domestic wastewater must comply with municipal sewer ordinances; confidential records and e-waste must be disposed through licensed operators in accordance with Ley 138 de 2013; indoor air and occupational exposure limits follow MITRADEL and CSS workplace safety thresholds.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Annual fire safety certification from the Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá (fire extinguishers, exits, and inspection), municipal structural and occupancy load clearance for the registered office, and workplace health and safety clearance from the Ministerio de Trabajo y Desarrollo Laboral (MITRADEL) for office employees.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF); electronic registration and filing portal: Sede Electrónica at https://sede.dgi.gob.pa with informational portal at https://www.dgi.gob.pa. Customs and Authorized Economic Operator (AEO) matters: Dirección General de Aduanas (DGA) through the Ventanilla Única de Comercio Exterior (VUCEN) and SISCOM.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned Panamanian Sociedad Anónima (S.A.) must obtain its RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente), which serves as the TIN for income tax, ITBMS, customs and AEO filings. Procedure: (1) incorporate by public deed (escritura pública) and register it in the Registro Público de Panamá; (2) appoint and confirm a resident agent (agente residente); (3) obtain the municipal Aviso de Operación (business license) from the district municipality of the registered office; (4) submit the RUC application through Sede Electrónica, or at a DGI service window, attaching the certified deed, resident-agent confirmation, legal representative sworn declaration, registered-office proof and the entity's statutory activity scope (ISIC 7020 management consultancy / supply-chain compliance audit); (5) upon RUC issuance, register as an ITBMS taxpayer when annual taxable turnover exceeds B/.36,000 and register as an employer with the Caja de Seguro Social (CSS) if personnel are hired; (6) use the same RUC for customs declarations through SISCOM/VUCEN and for AEO certification filings with the DGA.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Panama does not operate a check-the-box regime; the S.A. is automatically an entity-level taxpayer under the territorial system (Panama-source income taxed at 25%; foreign-source income exempt). Elections available: (1) Pequeño Contribuyente simplified regime for annual gross revenue up to B/.200,000 (Ley 74 de 2019); (2) RAD (Régimen Anticipado Definitivo), an elective definitive advance tax on gross receipts creditable against ISR; (3) Advance Pricing Agreements (APA) for transfer-pricing certainty with DGI; (4) election of monthly or quarterly ITBMS filing; (5) exporter credit/refund election for ITBMS saldo a favor; (6) no hybrid mismatch or consolidated filing elections recognized under Panama law.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS (Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios) — Panama's VAT/GST-equivalent transfer tax
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: B/.36,000 (Panamanian balboas, 1:1 with the US dollar) of aggregate annual taxable turnover from goods and services; any person exceeding this threshold during a fiscal year must register as an ITBMS taxpayer. Registration is also mandatory for any RUC-holder habitually performing taxable activities; taxpayers below the threshold may register voluntarily.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Panama mandates electronic invoicing (Facturación Electrónica) for all active taxpayers under DGI regulations. Invoices must be issued through the DGI's free e-invoicing platform or an authorized private service provider, transmitted to the DGI in XML format, and carry a unique DGI authorization code (código de autorización) and fiscal QR; the DGI performs real-time digital validation at issuance and pre-authorized numbering ranges are used only in approved offline scenarios. Invoices without DGI authorization are void for ITBMS credit purposes, non-deductible for ISR, and expose the issuer to fines. ITBMS returns and sworn declarations are filed exclusively through Sede Electrónica.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exports qualify for the 0% ITBMS rate when the goods physically leave Panama, title transfers to a non-resident buyer, and the exporter files a customs export declaration through SISCOM/VUCEN and repatriates the foreign-currency proceeds through the Panamanian banking system. Services, including AEO certification and supply-chain compliance audit services under ISIC 7020, are zero-rated where the recipient is a non-resident legal entity, the service is performed for use or exploitation wholly outside Panama, and the consideration is not attributable to Panama-source activities under the territorial test. The exporter must document contracts, work papers, performance-location memoranda, client due-diligence records and bank credit evidence. ITBMS input credits attributable to zero-rated exports are creditable against output ITBMS and any excess (saldo a favor) may be carried forward or refunded by the DGI. Panama does not codify a strict statutory repatriation date; the 180-day benchmark is applied in DGI and AEO supply-chain audit practice for foreign-exchange repatriation and profit-realization substance.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración de Exportación DUA) filed electronically through SISCOM/VUCEN
Bill of Lading (Conocimiento de Embarque), Airway Bill or equivalent transport document evidencing shipment from Panama
Inward Remittance Certificate / bank credit statement (Certificado de Ingreso de Divisas) evidencing collection of proceeds from abroad
Export commercial invoice (Factura Comercial) and financial settlement evidence
Packing List for goods; for services: original contract, foreign client master data, service performance report and place-of-consumption evidence
AEO certificate/customs authorization applicable to the export operation and security audit records
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The DGI and DGA jointly audit zero-rating claims and export documentation. Unsupported or fraudulent claims trigger: retrospective reassessment of the 7% ITBMS for the open prescription period (five years) plus monthly default interest, monetary fines up to 100% of the omitted tax under the Código Fiscal, criminal tax-fraud liability of two to five years' imprisonment for knowingly false declarations, cancellation of ITBMS refund/offset rights for all related periods, denial or revocation of AEO certification, and suspension of customs exporting privileges and of the S.A.'s paz y salvo (tax clearance) status.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: No formal central bank exists; Panama operates a dollarized monetary system. The Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP) regulates all banking activity, and Banco Nacional de Panamá acts as the fiscal agent for the government.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The US Dollar is legal tender alongside the Panamanian Balboa (PAB), which is a purely nominal unit at a 1:1 parity. There are no exchange controls or restrictions on current or capital account transactions. Profit remittances are freely permitted for properly constituted corporations; the only requirement is compliance with FATCA/CRS and anti-money laundering source-of-funds documentation. No separate capital controls exist.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender or mandatory conversion requirements exist for export receipts. Exporters are free to retain, transfer, or convert proceeds in any currency. Panama's territory-based tax system imposes no repatriation requirement.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low regulatory feasibility for offshore digital EMIs. Panama does not issue specialized Electronic Money Institution (EMI) licenses. Foreign EMIs such as Wise or Payoneer cannot maintain prohibited deposit-taking operations without a Panamanian banking license; however, their payment routing services can be used to disburse funds to Panamanian bank accounts via ACH or SWIFT. Such services are legally treated as payment processors, not local deposit-taking institutions, and may expose the company to non-bank counterparty risk. Recommended use is limited to minor operational outflows, not as a primary liquidity rail.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is typically required for the final signing of corporate resolutions and for the identification of directors and beneficial owners. Remote opening is permitted by some banks for non-resident directors only when the bank's compliance team conducts a video interview and all documentation is apostilled and legalized. In practice, most tier-1 banks demand at least one physical visit by the beneficial owner or an introduced attorney-in-fact with a notarized power of attorney.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High volume of cross-border payments to related foreign consulting entities
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide executed client engagement letters, detailed fee invoices with per-day work breakdown, underlying audit workpapers (redacted), and prior-year tax filings. Include bank statements of receiving entities to substantiate a clear funds trail.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Shareholder is a non-resident private interests foundation (PIF)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit the foundation's certificate of incorporation, its registered agent certificate, the foundation articles stamped by the Public Registry of Panama, and a recent good-standing certificate. Provide a beneficial ownership declaration form attested by the foundation's resident agent.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inconsistencies between business purpose (AEO audit services) and drawn-down capital
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Present a full business plan, projected profit-and-loss statements, the current supply chain compliance project pipeline, and vendor contracts. Disclose the origin of capital via notarized shareholder contribution certificates and bank-issued source-of-wealth references.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Signatory is a politically exposed person (PEP) or holds dual nationality outside FATF-approved jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Obtain an eligible legal opinion from a Panamanian law firm, a comprehensive CV with employment history, personal asset statements, sworn declarations, and PEP clearing consent. Provide references from a recognized banking institution for the preceding 12 months.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant wire transfer via SWIFT MT103 from the shareholder's own bank account to the Panamanian operational account. Purpose code 'B0500' (Business Services) or 'A9000' (Capital Investment) depending on whether the inflow is equity or trade advance. Inbound remittance instructions must clearly state the company name, ISIC 7020 AEO supply-chain audit contract reference, and the bank's BIC code. Verification requires a board resolution authorizing the injection, a share issuance certificate, and a formal capital contribution agreement. No exchange control approval is required.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For trade settlements, use standard commercial clearing rails: direct wire transfers (SWIFT MT103) for invoices and treaty payments; documentary commercial letters of credit (L/C) issued by a Panamanian bank for high-value non-standard procurements; and cross-border ACH (ACH Global) for recurring smaller vendor payments. All outbound disbursements must be supported by a valid invoice, a signed contract, and an AML-compliant source of funds record. Panama's efficient interbank clearing via SBP (Servicios Bancarios Panamá) ensures same-day local settlement.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright currency forwards (non-deliverable and deliverable) on USD/EUR and USD/JPY, available from authorized tier-1 banks
Cross-currency swaps (CCS) with maturity aligned to the AEO project cash flow
FX spot trades and simple over-the-counter (OTC) options for receiving non-USD advance payments
Plain vanilla interest rate swaps on credit facilities, if any

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual franchise tax payment (Tasa Única Anual de Matrícula)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) / Public Registry of Panama (Registro Público de Panamá)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before 30 June; assessed on a calendar-year basis irrespective of the incorporation anniversary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment after 30 June attracts a 10% surcharge plus monthly interest at the DGI statutory rate; the company is listed as irregular in the Public Registry, is barred from obtaining a good-standing certificate, and after three consecutive unpaid years may be administratively dissolved and struck off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) confirmation under Law 254 of 2021
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Public Registry of Panama – Beneficial Ownership Platform
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 30 June; an interim filing must be submitted within 15 business days after any change in beneficial ownership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or late filing exposes the company to administrative fines of up to USD 2,500 per occurrence, suspension of the good-standing certificate, and temporary suspension of the ability to register share transfers or corporate documents in the Public Registry; repeated non-compliance may support a strike-off application.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual resident agent sworn confirmation of corporate registers and registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Public Registry of Panama (via the licensed resident agent)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually as part of the 30 June franchise tax renewal cycle; also required within 15 business days of any change of registered office or registered agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: If the resident agent resigns without a successor being appointed, the company is immediately flagged as non-compliant and may be struck off after a one-year vacancy period; false or untimely confirmations may result in a fine against the resident agent and suspension of the company's active registry status.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A private Panama S.A. is not statutorily required to obtain an external audit unless (i) it is classified as a 'Gran Contribuyente' by the DGI, typically with annual taxable income in Panama of USD 2,500,000 or more; (ii) it is a licensed bank, insurer, trust company, or securities intermediary; or (iii) an audit is required by a creditor, customs/AEO authority, applicable foreign regulator, or the company's own bylaws. A non-licensed advisory S.A. operating below these thresholds may prepare unaudited internal financial statements.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Panamanian Fiscal Code requires accounting records sufficient to reflect assets, liabilities, income, and expenses; financial statements, when prepared, must comply with IFRS as adopted in Panama or, for eligible SMEs, the IFRS for SMEs framework.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Law 254 of 2021, every Panama-incorporated entity must identify its ultimate beneficial owner(s) and file a sworn declaration through the Public Registry's Beneficial Ownership Platform. The declaration must be filed at incorporation, upon any change in beneficial ownership within 15 business days, and at least once per calendar year even if ownership is unchanged. The resident agent is jointly responsible for verifying the underlying shareholding records and for submitting the annual confirmation on or before the 30 June deadline.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,800 – USD 4,200 for a small service entity, payable only when an audit is legally or contractually required

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% standard corporate income tax (ISR); a preferential 15% bracket applies to the first USD 50,000 of taxable income
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Territorial taxation: only Panama-source income (fees for AEO audits performed in Panama) is taxed; foreign-source fees excluded. Optional simplified RIT regime of 2% on gross receipts for taxpayers with gross annual revenue not exceeding USD 200,000. Net operating losses carried over 5 years, annual deduction capped at 20% of the subsequent year's net taxable income. No special CIT exemption for AEO consulting services.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 100 (Annual Corporate Income Tax Return) filed exclusively through the DGI e-tax platform (Sede Electrónica, TAT - Transferencia de Archivos Técnicos)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (Form 100) with quarterly advance income tax payments (Form 100-A) and monthly ITBMS VAT returns where applicable
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due within 90 days (3 months) after the fiscal year-end; calendar-year Sociedad Anónima must file on or before 31 March

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Aggregate Panama-source gross receipts from AEO certification, security audits and supply-chain compliance services; foreign-source audit fees earned and managed overseas must be reported in the non-taxable foreign-source annex, not in gross taxable revenue
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident-owned S.A. must include all revenues attributable to a fixed place of business or services rendered in Panama; fees from remote offshore AEO advisory work may be excluded under territoriality, provided the DGI's nexus requirements are met and supporting files are retained

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Direct costs and overheads necessary to earn taxable revenue (salaries, rent, third-party subcontractor fees, IT infrastructure); deductions must be documented by dated invoices and payroll remittances
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Management fees paid to a non-resident related company are deductible only if the service is real, economically substantiated and subject to the 15% non-resident WHT or treaty relief; the DGI may re-characterize a 'pass-through' commission as a dividend

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after applying the applicable 5-year loss carry-forward (max 20% of current net income per year) and any non-taxable foreign-source income separated as required
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A Sociedad Anónima electing territorial treatment must file the form plus a detailed source-of-income schedule to evidence that excluded service fees were performed outside Panama; this segregation is the principal audit trigger for DGI review

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Application of the 15% bracket to the first USD 50,000 of net taxable income and 25% on the excess; no additional surtax is levied for standard S.A. service businesses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For the 15%/25% stair-step, ensure cumulative bracket calculation; the DGI always recomputes this box automatically via the electronic system

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quarterly advance payments (usually 25% of the previous year's tax each), foreign tax credits if treaty-eligible, and withholding tax credits withheld by clients on invoices (e.g., 3% ISR on services rendered to the State or large taxpayers)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign tax credits are not available automatically; resident tax credit claims require the DGI-approved form and a tax-residency certificate from the source country

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final tax due after credits; payment must accompany the electronic filing via reference code, or a refund will be offset against future obligations
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders must ensure the company's tax balance is paid in full; a zero-liability return with an unpaid prior balance will trigger automatic garnishment of the S.A.'s Panamanian banking accounts

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: 5% monthly surcharge of the unpaid tax (maximum 50% of tax owed), plus statutory monthly interest on arrears; late filing of a nil return: fixed penalty of B/.50; false or fraudulent return: between B/.500 and B/.5,000 in addition to criminal confiscation, re-assessments and surcharges up to 100% of the omitted tax

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% final dividend withholding tax on any dividend or effective distribution paid by the S.A., including constructive dividends; 5% reduced WHT applies where dividends are paid from foreign-source income that was subject to effective Panamanian taxation (e.g., income remitted to Panama and taxed under the territorial regime)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Panama's DTA network (e.g., Mexico, Netherlands, Luxembourg, Spain, France, Portugal, Singapore, South Korea, Taiwan) allows full or partial relief on non-resident shareholders. Procedure: the payor must obtain the shareholder's tax-residency certificate (TRC), file the DGI beneficial-owner declaration, and embed the applicable treaty rate in the dividend voucher; TRCs are valid for the calendar year and must be updated annually; no treaty benefit without documentary evidence kept in Panama
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory WHT of 15% applies to royalty payments for the use of IP in Panama and to interest paid to non-resident lenders (General Tax Code Article 733); treaty rates normally reduce royalties to 5%–10% and interest to 0%–10%, subject to the TRC and beneficial-ownership protocol; interest on certain cross-border financing registered with the Superintendency of Banks may be exempt if so certified

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: USD 3,000,000: mandatory Local File for taxpayers whose annual gross revenue reaches this threshold; Master File and CbC Report required for MNE groups with consolidated group revenue ≥ USD 750,000,000; related-party transactions with entities in zero-tax or non-cooperative jurisdictions must be documented regardless of revenue threshold
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama adopted Economic Substance Notification (Law 70 of 2019, amended) requiring entities in an MNE group that perform 'relevant activities' (distribution and service center, headquarters, financing, leasing, shipping, IP holding) to file an annual economic-substance statement with the DGI and maintain local management, staff, premises and adequate expenditure. A pure AEO certification and audit company serving third-party clients may fall outside 'relevant activity'; however, if the S.A. acts as an intra-group back-office or regional compliance center, ESR filing and substance compliance are mandatory

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate underreporting of Panama-source AEO audit fees, use of fake offshore invoices to shift revenue offshore, or false beneficial-owner declarations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal tax fraud (defraudación fiscal) carries 2–5 years of imprisonment plus fines equal to the tax evaded and 40%–100% surcharge on omitted tax; DGI can also re-assess up to 5 years and seize funds from local accounts
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and authorized signatories who approved false returns are criminally liable as co-principals; courts may impose a travel ban (prohibition of leaving Panama), civil restitution of evaded tax plus damages, and, upon conviction, disqualification from managing companies in Panama

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a registered Sociedad Anónima with no real office, no local employees, no management activity in Panama, and routing AEO audit revenues without local substance while claiming treaty or territorial advantages
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DGI may disregard the S.A.'s separate existence, re-characterize inter-company payments as dividends, assess the 10% WHT plus 25% ISR and surcharges; the Commercial Registry may dissolve and cancel the company after repeated default; ESR certificate penalties up to B/.1,000,000 apply in regulated cases
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Under Panamanian corporate law, a court may pierce the veil when the S.A. is the alter ego of the shareholder or assets are commingled, making shareholders and directors personally liable for the company's tax debts and third-party claims; travel restrictions and denial of the annual municipal operating license may follow

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting undocumented client payments via Wire or Wise from tax-avoidance or sanctioned jurisdictions, or acting as an unlicensed intermediary for AEO-related security contraband or export-control evasion
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Sanctions under Law 23 of 2015 and the Financial Analysis Unit (UAF): fines up to USD 5,000,000 for non-licensed professionals participating in suspicion-free funds; money laundering is criminally punishable with 5–12 years' imprisonment and forfeiture of the underlying funds
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who ignore red flags become criminally liable (complicity in money laundering); preventive travel bans, asset freezes and bank-account locking by the Superintendency of Banks; a formal OFAC or UNSC designation in the AEO/customs audit chain would trigger cross-border arrest and extradition exposure

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Cross-border invoicing of AEO audit work to affiliated group entities at non-arm's-length fees, or payment of management fees to a related offshore service company without local substance, without TP documentation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The DGI may adjust income, disallow deductions, and impose a penalty of 40% of the tax omitted on transfer-pricing differences; late-payment interest at the statutory monthly rate and escalation to criminal tax fraud for deliberate manipulation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Signing officers who certified false TP analyses face personal administrative fines, claw-back of the adjusted tax from the corporate estate, and criminal exposure if the TP scheme was used to evade anti-money-laundering controls; travel bans are possible during tax-crimes prosecution
